title: RanLoRA nonlinear residual Mirror task-coordinate bank
hypothesis: With identical pretrained W, source-only calibration and same native nonlinear activation, an m-coded shared RanLoRA residual bank preserves native individually fitted RanLoRA task loss within 0.02 nat/token and reduces the complete multi-task residual adapter state >=15% at <=1.10x P95, beating an equal-byte native linear-code or diagonal Hadamard baseline.
native_method: RanLoRA's split of pretrained principal/residual singular directions, nonlinear rank-restricted residual adaptation and Hadamard modulation
physical_object: one frozen pretrained singular principal base plus a shared source-trained RanLoRA nonlinear residual operator bank
mirror_insertion: task-specific small Mirror m acting ONLY on the native nonlinear modulation vector / residual core, not a replacement of RanLoRA's main nonlinear path
synthetic_mechanism: Use a 64x64 frozen pretrained dense W, compute FP64 source-only singular basis; 6 naturalized source target nonlinear classification/regression tasks with common low-rank components, plus independent random private components at beta={0,0.3,0.8}. Two nonlinearity choices GELU/tanh fixed on dev. Teacher target outputs generated by independently initialized native residual adapters. Hold out whole target task generators and separate test inputs.
method_steps: (1) SVD W into frozen leading singular modes and tail, count all stored bases if not derived from checkpoint. (2) Implement native RanLoRA: adapt tail with low-rank factors followed by native nonlinear activation and elementwise modulation. (3) Fit source shared residual dictionary; freeze it. (4) Permit per-task support to learn small m, comparing diagonal/IA3 and rank-k ordinary linear core with identical paid state, plus optional r=1/2 private residual. (5) Train native full RanLoRA per task with same support and compute budget. (6) Audit function-space outputs, old-task interference, OOD shift and real serialized bytes; never infer quality from W Frobenius norm.
native_controls: Native individually fitted RanLoRA including its nonlinear Hadamard branch
Native RanLoRA with same-byte linear/spectral compressed task bank
RanLoRA plus ordinary diagonal per-task scaling
measurements: test per-task CE/RMSE, worst task, function-output Jacobian rank and retention, basis/code/private bytes, active GEMM/activation FLOPs and P95, percent trained improvement over native task zero-shot
hardware: CPU float32 64d toy; official RanLoRA LLM reproductions require GPU and exact source architecture; record fused vs eager kernel, dtype, training updates and separate factor storage.

gates.PASS: At least 4/5 fresh tasks mean task CE <=native RanLoRA+0.02 nat/token at <=0.85 total extra stored bytes and <=1.10 latency, with a strict benefit over same-byte ordinary task core and native diagonal Hadamard gate.
gates.FAIL: Plain RanLoRA, ordinary spectral/linear bank or diagonal scaling is Pareto-optimal; source task basis leaks target test factors; active nonlinear residual code costs more than source method.
gates.UNCERTAIN: native implementation unavailable, data contamination, missing bytes/quality/runtime or underpowered intervals

counterhypothesis: RanLoRA already contains nonlinear residual modulation. Mirror codes may only reparameterize its task gate and not provide additional useful degrees of freedom; broad private tasks may be off-orbit.
uncertainty: Spectral degeneracy and random basis sign, singular-value skew, source-tail mismatch, optimizer LR variation, numeric activation saturation; all comparisons on heldout function outputs.

accounting.storage: real serialized decoder/bank/code/cache/index/router metadata, no free shared bases
accounting.runtime: real hardware P50/P95, active compute and all copy/swap costs
